clue.text: The kind of society to appeal to a schoolboy?

definitions.text: The kind of society to appeal to a schoolboy?

parts.words: The kind of society to appeal to a schoolboy?
parts.note: a society without social ranks, read as a school day with fewer lessons, which any pupil would welcome

explanation.surface: A political question: what sort of society would a schoolboy vote for?
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a society without social ranks also splits as 'class' + 'less', which is what a pupil wants: fewer classes, meaning lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A society free of social hierarchy is described by this adjective.

clue.text: It sounds a good place to hide your money

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like another word, a homophone

parts.note: cash is money in hand

explanation.surface: Advice on where to stash your savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store or hiding place for valuables or supplies.

clue.text: He evidently gets satisfaction from his activities

definitions.text: He evidently gets satisfaction from his activities

parts.words: He evidently gets satisfaction from his activities
parts.note: satisfaction in its old sense of redress for a wrong, as one who takes revenge obtains

explanation.surface: A man who plainly enjoys what he does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satisfaction' looks like contentment; in its older sense it is repayment for an injury, which is what one who takes revenge exacts.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes revenge obtains satisfaction for a wrong done.

clue.text: Was Charity Pecksniff One of these ministering angels? 7

definitions.text: Was Charity Pecksniff One of these ministering angels?

parts.words: Was Charity Pecksniff One of these ministering angels?
parts.note: nursing nuns of a religious order, while Charity Pecksniff's sister in Martin Chuzzlewit is named ...

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Dickens character was a nursing nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Charity and Mercy are the two Pecksniff daughters in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, so Charity is literally a sister of Mercy; the phrase also names a Catholic order of nursing nuns. The '7' after the clue is only the enumeration's stray first figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious order of women devoted to nursing and service to the poor.

clue.text: It has capital support in architecture

definitions.text: It has capital support in architecture

parts.words: It has capital support in architecture
parts.note: in classical building, the horizontal section resting on the tops (capitals) of the columns

explanation.surface: Something in architecture that enjoys excellent backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital support' sounds like 'excellent backing'; a capital is the top of a column, and this upper part of a classical building rests on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The architrave, frieze and cornice above the columns of a classical building form this upper structure.

clue.text: A little drink, and this pet is in the soup

annotationWithheld.why: A little drink, and this pet is in the soup (3): 'A little drink' defines SIP, but no parse of 'this pet is in the soup' gives SIP with every word doing one job.
annotationWithheld.clue: A little drink, and this pet is in the soup

clue.text: What she takes part in is mainly dialogue

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about an actress whose role is mostly spoken lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'What she' included 'What', which only links; the girl's name is defined by 'she'. 'takes part in' tells you the name sits inside 'mainLY DIAlogue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it can stand for any female person referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: One of Elgar's major variations ?

indicators.note: Elgar wrote the Enigma Variations, and here the word says his name's letters are varied, rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Asks about one of the big pieces in Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variations' recalls Elgar's Enigma Variations but rearranges the letters of ELGAR; 'One of' and the question mark just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean big or great in size or importance.

clue.text: Literary giant who may be praised

indicators.note: says the clue word could become something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great writer worthy of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary giant' suggests a great author; it is a real giant, the one in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress who keeps Doubting Castle. 'may be' rearranges PRAISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Despair imprisons Christian and Hopeful in Doubting Castle in Bunyan's allegory.

clue.text: This pear is the avocado

parts.note: an old name for the avocado is a pear named after a large reptile, from its rough green skin

explanation.surface: A fruit seller's statement identifying a pear variety.
explanation.walkthrough: The avocado was once called the 'alligator pear', from its knobbly green skin; the clue asks for the word before 'pear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is also known as the alligator pear, from its bumpy reptilian skin.

clue.text: A kind of light basket

parts.note: an iron basket filled with burning fuel to give illumination, not a basket that weighs little

explanation.surface: A lightweight basket, as for picnics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like 'not heavy'; it is illumination, since this is an iron fire basket used as a torch or beacon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a metal container holding burning oil or coal, used as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Sunday's put-up job ?

parts.note: a shade raised against the sun, split as sun-day: the job the sun gives to something that is put up

explanation.surface: Suggests a Sunday swindle or a rigged affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put-up job' means a fraud, but here it is literal: the thing you put up for the sun's sake. 'Sunday' is read as the day of strong sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is opened (put up) to shield someone from the sun's rays.

clue.text: It sustains Holy Writ in the church

definitions.text: It sustains Holy Writ in the church

parts.words: It sustains Holy Writ in the church
parts.note: a church lectern is often carved as a bird with spread wings on which the Bible rests

explanation.surface: Something that keeps scripture alive in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustains' means 'holds up' physically: many church lecterns are shaped as a bird of prey bearing the Bible on its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecterns in churches are traditionally made in the form of this bird, carrying the Bible.

clue.text: One expected to make a come-back

definitions.text: One expected to make a come-back

parts.words: One expected to make a come-back
parts.note: a curved throwing stick designed to return to the thrower

explanation.surface: Sounds like a fallen sports star tipped for a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come-back' suggests a celebrity's return; it is literal, since this Australian throwing stick flies back to the hand that threw it.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved Aboriginal throwing weapon is shaped so that it returns to its thrower.

clue.text: Togged up for cricket-excessively so !

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
togged up is British slang for dressed

explanation.surface: Someone kitted out for a cricket match far too elaborately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cricket' seems to describe a player's kit, but it supplies a cricket term placed in front; 'excessively so' then means dressed too much, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing clothes too formal or elaborate for the occasion is this state.

clue.text: It sounds anything but a stuffy town

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like another word, a homophone

parts.note: fresh air is the opposite of a stuffy atmosphere

explanation.surface: A town described as anything but dull and airless.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR is a town on the west coast of Scotland. The word heard is AIR, the very opposite of stuffiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish seaside town and former county seat in Ayrshire.

clue.text: One Shavian role, and others — about a hundred

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer letters surround the inner one

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
S, the plural ending, stands for more of the same

explanation.surface: A list of parts in a Shaw play, with about a hundred extras.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero of Shaw's play Androcles and the Lion. 'about' puts C inside ROLES, giving ROCLES after AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcles is the title character of George Bernard Shaw's play Androcles and the Lion.

clue.text: It's certainly not the way to keep it !

definitions.text: It's certainly not the way to keep it

parts.words: It's certainly not the way to keep it
parts.note: a confidential government matter, read as an instruction to announce something private, which defeats keeping it

explanation.surface: Advice that some approach will not preserve something.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun phrase for classified government information also reads as a verb plus object: 'state a secret', i.e. declare it, which is no way to keep it.
explanation.definitionFit: Information withheld by the government for security reasons is known by this phrase.

clue.text: Little Edward putting on weight does light duty

parts.note: Eddy is a familiar short form of the name Edward
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A small boy gaining weight while doing only easy chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light duty' sounds like easy work; it means serving as a light, since this is the famous lighthouse off Plymouth. A stone is a British unit of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The lighthouse on the Eddystone Rocks off Plymouth guides shipping with its beam.

clue.text: At a loss for words-silly set up

parts.note: dumb is informal for stupid or silly
to found a business is to set it up

explanation.surface: Someone speechless, feeling foolish about an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astonished to the point of speechlessness is this state.

clue.text: Wild women, writing about a wild Dane

indicators.note: about means going round, so the writing's letters surround what follows

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unruly women writing about an unruly Danish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild women' are the frenzied followers of Dionysus in Greek myth. 'wild' rearranges the Dane, and 'about' puts the writing's abbreviation around A plus that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied female followers of the god Dionysus in Greek myth, hence any frenzied women.

clue.text: A sound receptacle

parts.note: an organ that receives sounds, rather than a container in good condition

explanation.surface: A container in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'in good repair'; it is noise, and the receptacle for noise is the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing takes in sound waves.

clue.text: Passed, was terribly pleased

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly knocked about, so its letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who passed a test and was overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' looks like success in an exam; it means gone by, of time. 'was terribly' rearranges PLEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: When time has gone by, it is said to have done this.

clue.text: It's apparent in this place, yonder

parts.note: overt means open and plainly apparent
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A remark that something is visible right here and also far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at that place in the distance, as opposed to nearby.

clue.text: The part of the joint a number gets on with

parts.note: ten is a number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer's turn in a nightclub, with the act getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a nightclub; it is a woodwork joint, and this is the projecting tongue that fits into the mortise.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry, the projecting piece shaped to fit into a mortise to form a joint.

clue.text: Mass migration from the sweet-stuff factory ?

definitions.text: Mass migration from the sweet-stuff factory

parts.words: Mass migration from the sweet-stuff factory
parts.note: the hive makes honey, the sweet stuff, and bees leave it in a great cluster

explanation.surface: Workers leaving a confectionery plant all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sweet-stuff factory' is a beehive making honey; a mass of bees leaving it with a new queen is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of honeybees leaving the hive together to found a new colony is called this.

clue.text: See 3
He has an initial distinction in driving

definitions.text: He has an initial distinction in driving

parts.words: He has an initial distinction in driving
parts.note: a novice driver in Britain is marked out by the letter L on plates on the car

explanation.surface: A driver who earned top marks early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial distinction' sounds like an early honour; it is a distinguishing initial letter, the red L plate a British novice driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still being taught to drive displays L plates in the UK.

clue.text: Eve was a bit ticklish at first

definitions.text: Eve was a bit ticklish at first

parts.words: Eve was a bit ticklish at first
parts.note: in Genesis the first woman was made from a bone taken from Adam's side, and to tease someone is another sense of the word

explanation.surface: Eve was rather sensitive to tickling in the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' reads as 'initially'; it means at Creation, when Eve began as a bone from Adam's side. The answer also means to tease, which is a kind of ticklishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says Eve was formed from a bone of Adam's side, and to tease someone is also this word.

clue.text: Undertaker at a christening

parts.note: a godparent, who undertakes promises on the baby's behalf, not a funeral director

explanation.surface: A funeral director oddly present at a baptism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaker' suggests a funeral director; it means one who undertakes, as a godparent makes vows for the child at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent at a baptism takes on obligations for the child, which is this role.

clue.text: A Dickensian nipper

parts.note: Nipper is the surname of a sharp-tongued maid in Dickens's Dombey and Son, not a child

explanation.surface: A child from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like British slang for a small child; it is the surname of Florence Dombey's maid in Dombey and Son, whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The maid in Dombey and Son has the first name asked for and the surname Nipper.

clue.text: A wild duet, by Gad ! Now for the Chancellor's solo

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so these letters run in a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a wild musical duet, then a switch to a political solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges DUET BY GAD. The Chancellor of the Exchequer delivers the annual Budget speech to Parliament alone, hence 'solo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual occasion when Britain's finance minister presents tax plans to Parliament in a single speech.
